points.description: The compressed data rate must not exceed the communication channel capacity, while using the full capacity of the channel (i.e. the rate is matched to the channel capacity). Equivalent wording, such as 'the output rate should fit within the channel bandwidth and use it fully', earns the mark.

Maximum quality of the data must be preserved (i.e. the compression should be as close to lossless or as high-quality as possible). Equivalent wording, such as 'minimal loss of information' or 'best possible fidelity', earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Full marks for a student who names both the channel-capacity constraint (rate not exceeding capacity and fully utilising it) and the preservation of maximum quality. Award 1 mark for each idea and 0 for an answer that omits it or gives an unrelated issue. The two capacity statements are treated as one idea, so there is no partial credit.
